title: Slotted priority decayer: slot allocator for continuous batching to reduce starvation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a slotted priority allocator for the continuous batcher to improve fairness and reduce starvation; adds jittered timeout gates and KV cache pin timeouts to avoid head-of-line blocking.
description:
Context and motivation: Continuous batching has improved throughput but we still observe rare long-tail request starvation when a small set of high-cost KV-heavy requests monopolize the in-memory slot pool. Existing priority escalations were too aggressive (starving background classes) or too static (unable to react to transient spikes). This PR implements a slotted priority-decayer allocator that gives short, reclaimable "slots" to higher-priority requests while decaying their effective priority over time so that long-running or repeated high-cost requests gracefully yield to waiting lower-priority traffic. The goal is to reduce observed 99.9th latency tail without regressing median throughput.

Summary of changes (single-string commit summary):
- Add SlotAllocator and PriorityDecayer components to runtime scheduler.
- Implement jittered slot timeouts and backoff to avoid synchronized evictions.
- Add per-tenant max-wait heuristics and a soft preemption path for pinned KV cache entries.
- Introduce metrics and tracing points for slot acquisition/release and starvation events.
- Tweak kernel hinting to prefer fused kernels for short-sequence KV-heavy microbatches.
- Tests: unit & integration tests for fairness, starvation scenarios, and a small load test harness.

Commits (high level):
1) feat(scheduler): initial slotted allocator implementation (slot_allocator.rs + interfaces) — Maya
2) perf(scheduler): add priority decayer logic + jittered timeouts — Maya
3) feat(kv): soft-unpin hook and TTL for pinned KV entries (kv_cache.rs) — Maya
4) test(scheduler): add starvation regression tests and load harness — Maya
5) docs: add design note and observability docs for allocator behavior — Maya
6) fix(tests): flake in scheduler_timeout_test caught and addressed — Maya

Files changed (high-level, illustrative):
- runtime/scheduler/slot_allocator.rs
- runtime/scheduler/priority_decayer.rs
- runtime/scheduler/mod.rs (wiring & interfaces)
- runtime/kv/kv_cache.rs (soft-unpin, pin_ttl)
- runtime/telemetry/metrics.rs (new metrics)
- runtime/tests/allocator_starvation_test.rs
- examples/benchmarks/continuous_batcher_starve_sim.rs
- docs/design/slot_allocator.md
- docs/observability/slot_metrics.md

Small illustrative snippets (kept minimal):
- slot timeout jittering: "let timeout = base_timeout + rng.sample(jitter); // prevents herd eviction"
- decayer update: "priority = priority * exp(-decay_rate * held_slots)"

Design notes and rationale: The slotted model treats the continuous batcher pool as a set of reclaimable slots rather than exclusive worker tokens. When a request acquires a slot it is given a soft TTL. High-priority requests receive shorter but immediate slots; if they retain the slot beyond the TTL their effective priority is decayed so queued lower-priority requests eventually get scheduled. This prevents pathological starvation where a few expensive requests keep re-occupying slots. Jittered TTLs ensure evictions are spread to avoid synchronized thundering-herd re-requests. The allocator also exposes a soft preemption hook: when a tenant exceeds max-wait for a request class, the scheduler may trigger soft-unpin on heavily pinned KV entries, allowing progress for waiting traffic at the cost of cache churn — this is controlled by tenant-configurable heuristics.

Observability and metrics: Added metrics:
- scheduler.slot_acquire_total
- scheduler.slot_release_total
- scheduler.slot_evicted_jittered_total
- scheduler.priority_decay_events
- scheduler.tenant_max_wait_exceeded
Tracing spans added for allocation lifecycle and soft-unpin windows. Design doc and observability pages added in docs/ to help SRE tune decay_rate, base_timeout, and jitter width per workload.

Testing and CI: Initial CI run failed on scheduler_timeout_test due to a race in the test harness (timing assumptions vs jitter). Fixed by making the test assert ranges rather than absolute timings and adding a retry harness for flaky timing. Comprehensive unit tests added for decayer math, integration tests simulate mixed KV-light and KV-heavy load with per-tenant QoS and assert no starvation for 30s windows in the harness. Local perf tests show 15-22% reduction in 99.9th latency for our KV-heavy synthetic workload with <3% median throughput regression in the tightest configs.

Review conversation (condensed into a single string):
- Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Nice approach — treated slots as reclaimable is a good mental model. Two asks: add a feature flag and ensure decay parameters are tenant-configurable via runtime config. Also please add a microbenchmark for the decayer math to prove negligible CPU overhead." 
- Maya Chen (author): "Added feature flag (experimental.slotted_allocator) and made decay_rate / base_timeout tenant overridable; added microbenchmark in runtime/bench/decayer_bench.rs." 
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Concern about KV soft-unpin causing cache churn on hot slots — can we gate on pin_count > threshold and add a cooldown to avoid repeated churn?" 
- Maya Chen: "Added a cooldown window and pin_count threshold check; documented tradeoffs in docs/design/slot_allocator.md." 
- Sofia Martinez (SRE reviewer): "Metrics look good. Please ensure the slot eviction metric is tagged with tenant_id and model to help debugging." 
- Maya Chen: "Added tenant/model tags to eviction and max_wait metrics."
- Arjun Patel: "Approving pending small nit on a log line formatting (fixed)."
- Merge: "squash and merge" after CI green.

CI matrix summary: unit tests (linux) = pass, integration (kitchen) = pass, lint (clippy/format) = pass, perf smoke = pass. One rerun after the timing flake; all checks green on final.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan: This feature is behind an experimental feature-flag. Default disabled on main. Rollout plan:
1) Canary (10% of traffic) with feature flag enabled and elevated observability (1h window) — monitor slot_evicted_jittered_total and tenant_max_wait_exceeded.
2) If stable at canary, enable for more tenants and reduce decay aggressiveness for latency-sensitive customers.
3) For Dedicated/Private customers requiring stability, this stays opt-in until verified.

Follow-ups: (a) Auto-tune decay_rate based on observed retry/backoff patterns (ENG-8489), (b) tighter kernel hinting integration to preferentially route short-seq KV-heavy microbatches to the fused kernel path (performance win observed in local bench).

Notes: No breaking API changes. Configurable knobs added to runtime config are documented; defaults are conservative. The merged patch increases code paths in scheduler but keeps previous behavior by default when the feature flag is off.
